findings.F1: Fees eat the gain: the position earns 0.000826 per bar before costs and pays 0.000706 per bar in fees on a turnover of 0.65 of the book per bar, so the book's daily mean is 0.000103 against holding's 0.001180.
findings.F2: The fade loses after costs in every volatility state except the most turbulent. Split by the coin's 20-day volatility against its 120-bar mean absolute move, the four lowest sextiles net -0.000706 to -0.001039 per bar (t -1.15 to -1.87, about 1480 bars each), the fifth nets 0.000429 (t 0.43), and only the top sextile (ratio 2.25) nets 0.003212 (t 3.49).
findings.F3: Even in calm sextiles the book carries mean |position| 0.30 to 0.46 and pays fees of 0.00050 to 0.00077 per bar, so the forecast's grading does not shrink exposure enough where there is no edge.
findings.F4: The short side carries the losses. Short bars earn 0.000261 timing per bar against 0.001481 for long bars (about 8.4k to 8.9k bars each). In the high-volatility tercile shorts net -0.000226 per bar while longs net 0.004040 (t 4.52, n 1408).
findings.F5: Shorting an up day while the coin's 20-day return is up is the worst case: net -0.001477 per bar (t -2.95, n 4089). Buying a down day nets 0.001187 in a 20-day downtrend (t 2.52) and 0.001265 in an uptrend (t 2.88).
findings.F6: The result depends on the period. Inside the top two volatility sextiles net is negative in 9 of 23 windows (for example w12 -0.0065, w17 -0.0049, w21 -0.0040), and outside them it is negative in 16 of 24. This matches the failed leave-one-window-out Sharpe of -0.081 and the Calmar of -0.048.

ideas.idea: A coin whose last day's move was large relative to its 20-day volatility moves the opposite way over the next 1 day, and the reversal is larger the larger that scaled move and the higher the coin's 20-day volatility stands against its own history, only while its 20-day volatility stands well above its own 120-day average daily move.
ideas.consequence: Fade violent days only in clearly turbulent stretches and stay out otherwise, so the book stops paying fees on calm-market fades that earn nothing.
ideas.name: reversal only in turbulence

ideas.idea: A coin whose last day's move was large relative to its 20-day volatility moves the opposite way over the next 1 day, and the reversal is larger the larger that scaled move and the higher the coin's 20-day volatility stands against its own history, except after an up day, when the coin keeps the drift it had over its last 20 days.
ideas.consequence: Buy the bounce after violent down days in turbulent markets, but do not short violent up days, especially in a rising market.
ideas.name: violent falls rebound next day
